New evidence from today: this is not a pure session created on the wrong server problem.

I attached the TUI directly to the 4096 server and created a brand new session in Lara47.

Command used:
opencode attach http://192.168.0.101:4096 --dir C:\Users\attila\Projects\Lara47\

Then I verified the result against the 4096 API itself.

The 4096 server does return the new Lara47 session correctly:
- GET /session?directory=C:\Users\attila\Projects\Lara47&roots=true&limit=10
- includes session ses_2d158eabdffeYZbiLQsZneCu46
- projectID = e06f5f1373bbadc24eac6873ebd27550f5092612
- directory = C:\Users\attila\Projects\Lara47

So for this reproduction, the session is definitely created on and listed by the 4096 server.

But in Desktop, the same session still only appears under Lokaler Server, not under the 192.168.0.101:4096 sidebar.

That means at least this Lara47 reproduction is much closer to #17451 and #18302 territory:
- server-side creation is correct
- server-side listing is correct
- the failure is in Desktop or WebUI server-context isolation or sidebar state, where server plus directory is apparently not being separated cleanly

So my current reading is:
- there may still be an additional project-scoping or path-normalization problem in some repos, for example OpCo-Know had earlier API-level oddities
- but this new Lara47 attach reproduction is a clean proof that one important failure mode is client-side server-context collision, not session creation on the wrong server

Workaround: How to recover archived sessions right now

Archived sessions are not deleted. They live in OpenCode's local SQLite database at ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db. Archiving just sets a time_archived timestamp on the row. Clearing it brings the session back. Two ways to fix this:

Method 1: Give this prompt to your coding agent (easiest)

Paste this into a new OpenCode session (or any coding agent with terminal access) and it will handle everything:

My archived OpenCode chat sessions are missing from the sidebar. They are stored in the SQLite database at ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db in the session table. The column time_archived is set to a timestamp when a session is archived. To restore them, set time_archived = NULL.

Do this:

Run a read-only query first to show me all sessions where time_archived IS NOT NULL. Display the session ID, title, created date, and archived date in a readable format.
Ask me whether I want to restore all of them, or just specific ones.
Run the appropriate UPDATE query to set time_archived = NULL on the sessions I choose.
Verify the update by confirming zero archived sessions remain (or only the ones I excluded).
Tell me to restart OpenCode so the sessions reappear in the sidebar.
That's it. The agent will walk you through the recovery interactively, just like a human would.

Method 2: Manual terminal commands

If you prefer doing it yourself:

See your archived sessions:

sqlite3 ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db \
  "SELECT id, title, datetime(time_created/1000, 'unixepoch') as created, datetime(time_archived/1000, 'unixepoch') as archived FROM session WHERE time_archived IS NOT NULL ORDER BY time_archived DESC;"
Restore a single session:

sqlite3 ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db \
  "UPDATE session SET time_archived = NULL WHERE id = 'ses_XXXXX';"
Restore all archived sessions for one project:

# Find your project ID first
sqlite3 ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db "SELECT id, directory FROM project;"

# Then restore
sqlite3 ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db \
  "UPDATE session SET time_archived = NULL WHERE project_id = 'YOUR_PROJECT_ID' AND time_archived IS NOT NULL;"
Restore everything across all projects:

sqlite3 ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db \
  "UPDATE session SET time_archived = NULL WHERE time_archived IS NOT NULL;"
Then restart OpenCode. Sessions will reappear in the sidebar.

Why this is safe

Only the time_archived column is changed. No messages, code diffs, or content is touched.
SQLite uses WAL mode here, so writes are crash-safe.
You can re-archive sessions from the UI anytime.
sqlite3 is pre-installed on macOS and most Linux distros. Windows users can get it from [sqlite.org/download](https://sqlite.org/download.html).
How it works under the hood

The session table has a nullable column time_archived INTEGER. The UI filters out any row where this value is not null. Setting it back to NULL is all it takes to make the session visible again. Nothing is ever truly deleted by archiving.

Tested and confirmed working as of March 2026 on macOS. The database path follows XDG conventions, so on Linux it's the same ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db.

I've been testing it locally against a real-world use case (a plugin that creates git worktrees and binds sessions to them) and can confirm it fixes the core issue: tools now correctly operate in the session's stored directory rather than `Instance.directory`.

However, there's one gap: plugin tool context is not updated

In `packages/opencode/src/tool/registry.ts`, when a plugin-registered tool's `execute` function is called, the `ToolContext` passed to it is constructed like this:

```
const pluginCtx = {
  ...toolCtx,
  directory: ctx.directory,   // <-- still uses Instance context, not session directory
  worktree: ctx.worktree,
}
```

`ctx.directory` here comes from the `InstanceContext` captured at init time, it reflects the directory OpenCode was started with, not the session's directory. This means that while all built-in tools (bash, read, edit, glob, grep, etc.) will correctly use `Session.directory.get()` after this PR, any tool registered by a plugin will still receive the startup directory in its `ToolContext.directory`.

This matters for any plugin that:
- uses `context.directory` to resolve file paths or execute commands
- creates child processes scoped to the session's working directory
- makes decisions based on the current project directory (e.g., reading project config, resolving relative paths, interacting with git)

Essentially, any plugin that relies on `ToolContext.directory` to know "where am I operating" would get stale information for sessions with custom directories (worktrees, sandboxes, or any session created via the API with a directory query parameter).

The fix would be a one-liner in `registry.ts`:

```
 const pluginCtx = {
   ...toolCtx,
-  directory: ctx.directory,
+  directory: Session.directory.get(),
   worktree: ctx.worktree,
 }
 ```

with the corresponding import:
```
+import { Session } from "../session"
```

This ensures plugin tools get the same per-session directory that built-in tools use, maintaining consistency across the entire tool surface.

I've tested this additional change locally alongside the rest of the PR and it works as expected — plugin tools receive the correct worktree path when operating within a session that has a custom directory.

I'm definitely in agreement with this final section of this issue https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/8936. I felt the scope of the ticket was too narrow for what I wanted to discuss but the final point is good.

- At every level if an allow rule exists then anything that is not allowed should be denied.
Mixed allow and deny rules are only useful with glob patterns to explicitly deny a more specific case that would otherwise be allowed.
- Any matching deny pattern when globbing should always short circuit and prevent the tool from running. No later pattern can override this except perhaps for a strict direct match with no globbing.

```yaml
bash
- "rm *": allow # allows rm commands
- "rm *-rf*": deny # denies any rm command with -rf in it
- "rm -rf node_modules": allow # allows this exact command (CAN supersede a glob deny)
- "rm -rf node_modules*": allow # can never override the deny rule because it includes a glob
```

This seems to me to be the only sane approach to security in this case.

I had the same issue today with OpenCode CLI on Linux. It seems OpenAI refreshed the limits and invalidated the token, so I started getting this error: `Forbidden: request was blocked by a gateway or proxy. You may not have permission to access this resource — check your account and provider settings`.
I ran `opencode auth logout` and then `opencode auth login`. The browser showed that authentication was successful, but the OpenCode logs said: `Token exchange failed`.
The main problem was that I have to use a VPN to work with ChatGPT, and my VPN client creates several `*_proxy` environment variables when is started. Those work fine with OpenCode authentication, but I made one mistake: I ran the terminal and `opencode` command BEFORE starting the VPN client, so the terminal session didn't see new environment vars.
So the solution is very simple: start the VPN, reopen the terminal, and only then run `opencode auth login`.
Thanks to @fastknifes for the link, it helped me to fix my issue.

This is more complicated than it sounds. I used @zer0Black's approach to force OpenCode to answer in my native language (Spanish), even when all the prompts used by OpenCode are in English. It works, sort of. I noticed a drop in quality and certain English cultural biases, like an answer referenced pounds, when every Spanish speaking country in the world uses the metric system.

It turns out there is a price to pay for mixing languages. Benchmarks such as [this one](https://lilt.com/blog/multilingual-llm-performance-gap-analysis) show that there is reduction in output quality.

Some solutions have being explored in [here](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.11665) or [here](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.11056v2), the most complex ideas would require some coding, but some of the basic ones can be used in OpenCode as it is today.

This are some of the strategies available in OpenCode:

- Ask the LLM to produce output in Spanish
- Translate the output to Spanish after the fact
- Translate prompts to English, and the answer back to Spanish
- Translate the agent prompt

The first 3 can be done by modifying AGENTS.md accordingly, but the back and forth of the translation step will consume extra tokens. The last one requires to modify [OpenCode's configuration](https://opencode.ai/docs/agents/#prompt).
